HAGONOY, Bulacan — More than 300 residents marched through the streets of this municipality early Sunday to mark the first anniversary of Tindig Hagonoy, renewing their call for justice over alleged corruption in flood control projects and for concrete solutions to the town’s chronic flooding problem.

The protesters also called for accountability over the alleged billion-peso “ghost” flood control projects they blamed for worsening flooding that has repeatedly submerged much of the town, leaving residents helpless.

A year after Tindig Hagonoy first staged organized a march through flooded streets to protest alleged corruption in flood control projects, Saguinsin said residents are now waiting for the national government to deliver solutions, following assurances from Public Works and Highways Secretary Vince Dizon.
Tindig Kalumpitenyo organized the People’s Rally for the second consecutive year, with more than 300 residents and various groups joining the demonstration.

The mass action, which began with a dawn Mass and a program at the town plaza, was held to denounce alleged corruption in multibillion-peso flood-control projects that residents say have left their coastal town submerged and suffering.

Yuda was among hundreds of residents from various sectors—fisherfolk, tricycle drivers, students, youth groups, professionals, church leaders, persons with disabilities, artists, and fraternity members—who spoke during the Sept. 20 “Black Saturday” protest rally called Tindig Hagonoy.

Lucia, Bulusan, Calizon, Gugo, Iba Oeste, Caniogan, Frances, Meysulao, and San Miguel, all in Calumpit are under one to five feet water, according to the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction Management Office.

CITY OF MALOLOS, Bulacan – At least 21 barangays in the towns of Hagonoy and Calumpit, this province on Monday have been submerged in floodwaters due to rains brought by Typhoon Quinta and aggravated by the high tide from the Manila Bay.
Lyn Ching aired her frustrations over the prolonged flooding in Hagonoy, Bulacan, saying residents have been dealing with floodwaters for about two years.
